prerequisites: Ability to understand and speak Euskera and master its grammatical rules (approximately C1 level).
It is advisable, but not mandatory, to have completed 'Written Scientific-Technical Communication in Euskera (IKZTE)'.

learning_outcomes.text: Recognize that within a same linguistic system there are multiple variants of use, differentiate between general language and specialized language, to adequately use the linguistic resources proper to each use.
Become aware of the determining steps for the development of languages.
Know the current situation of Euskera to raise awareness among university graduates about its use and its impact on development.
Have basic linguistic knowledge and criteria to guarantee the linguistic quality of engineering texts.
Knowledge of digital and paper linguistic resources and, above all, critical capacity to use and complement these resources.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, make decisions, use creativity, reason critically and communicate and transmit knowledge and skills.
Ability to draft and develop projects in the field of Engineering.
Ability to work in a linguistic and multidisciplinary environment.
Maintain a responsible and orderly work attitude and be willing to learn at all times.
Awareness of the influence of higher education graduates on the use and development of Euskera and the review of personal communicative role in this context.
The search, comprehension, synthesis and critical analysis of scientific information.
Agree, present and argue ways to address problems related to research, technical advice and teaching, through collaboration.
The use of consultation tools, particularly those available on the Internet, to adequately respond to the needs that may arise in different communication situations.

Modify topics related to science, taking into account the demands of the communicative context: popular science lectures, master classes, congress communications, written support for conferences, scientific posters.
Systematize, explain and review one's own linguistic intuitions and experiences.

syllabus_topics: MODULE 1: Language management in a multilingual academic and professional environment
Linguistic rights and minority languages.
Minority languages and language planning.
Planning the standardization of Euskera.
Language contact, loanwords, calques, and linguistic dependence.
Good practices in language management in a multilingual academic and professional context.
Attentive listening.
Reading and debate of various reference documents.
Presentations.
MODULE 2: Linguistic variants and speakers' linguistic repertoire
Linguistic variants: geographical variants vs functional variants.
Variability in oral registers.
Formal pronunciation of Batua Euskera.
Linguistic repertoire and formal communication of speakers.
Comparison of written and oral texts.
Punctuation vs prosody.
Identification of formal pronunciation in scientific videos.
From written text to oral reading.
MODULE 3: Discursive strategies for oral communication
Persuasion in academic and professional multimodal communication.
Rhetorical resources: rhetorical questions, repetition, exemplification, reformulation.
Phonetic resources: pauses, intonation.
Non-verbal resources.
Oral communication for didactic purposes: master class, video tutorial, popular science talk.
MODULE 4: Functional language of Euskera in the academic field
Revitalization of minority languages: specialized terminology and phraseology.
Development of academic registers of Euskera.
Variability in developed languages and those undergoing normalization.
Implementation of specialized linguistic resources in expert discourses.
Academic and popular science textual genres: presentation of academic works, popular science conference, poster.
teaching_methods: Analysis of the initiation procedure for GRAL
assessment_rules: Continuous evaluation requires attendance at all sessions and timely submission of all tasks. Students have the right to be evaluated by final evaluation, regardless of participation in continuous evaluation, by submitting a written waiver within nine weeks from the start of the semester. Students who withdraw from the call will receive a 'pending presentation' grade; if the final test weighs over 40% in continuous evaluation, non-appearance is sufficient for this grade. The extraordinary call will assess learning outcomes through an exam in the same format as the ordinary call, with a value of 100%, consisting of questions/tests/exercises (40%), presentation (40%), and oral reading (20%).
